title: Hand of Straights
summary: Alice possesses a set of cards numbered in an array.
statement: Alice possesses a set of cards numbered in an array. She aims to organize these cards into groups of equal size, where each group contains consecutive card numbers of the specified size. Given the card values in an array and the group size, determine if Alice can successfully arrange the cards as required, returning true if possible, otherwise false.
constraints: Every card must belong to a group of group_size consecutive values.
hints: The smallest remaining card must start a group because no smaller predecessor can consume it.
Process values ascending and remove all copies of each start from its consecutive range.
For copies=count[start], subtract copies from start..start+size-1, rejecting shortages.
The forced smallest choice is safe; batching equal starts handles duplicates without changing the greedy proof.
editorial: The forced smallest choice is safe; batching equal starts handles duplicates without changing the greedy proof.

tests.explanation: Five cards cannot be divided into groups of four.
